questions.q: Which aldehyde does NOT undergo the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH?
questions.explain: Acetaldehyde has α-hydrogens, so strong base forms its enolate faster than it adds to the carbonyl, and aldol products result. The other three lack α-hydrogen.

questions.q: A mixture of benzaldehyde and formaldehyde is warmed with concentrated NaOH. The main products are:
options: Benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate only
questions.explain: In a crossed Cannizzaro reaction the cheap HCHO acts as the hydride donor and is oxidised to formate, while the valuable aldehyde is reduced to its alcohol in high yield.

questions.q: Under normal conditions the rate law and overall order of the Cannizzaro reaction are:
questions.explain: Two aldehyde molecules and one hydroxide are involved, giving third-order kinetics. The fourth-order term (second order in OH⁻) appears only at very high base concentration, via the dianion.

questions.q: Acetaldehyde is treated with excess formaldehyde and base. The final organic product (besides formate) is:
questions.explain: Three aldol additions of HCHO use up all three α-hydrogens, giving (HOCH₂)₃C–CHO; having no α-H left, it is then reduced by a fourth HCHO in a crossed Cannizzaro reaction. Stopping at the trihydroxy aldehyde is the trap.
